subject: Crest5b: increased timeouts & elevated error-rate — status and remediation
messages:
From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@brightlayer.app>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <pshah@brightlayer.app>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Crest5b production timeouts (us-west) — urgent

Hi Evelyn —

We started seeing a spike in timeouts and 5xx responses from the model endpoint crest5b in our us-west cluster around 07:50 PST this morning. Impact: our customer-facing chat flow (session IDs prefixed BL-) began failing to return completions, and our retry logic is being exhausted. We observed ~12% 5xx rate and a corresponding uptick in 1.2s+ tail latencies.

I attached a small slice of request/response logs (crest5b-sample-logs-20261214.tar.gz) and a short synthetic timeline. Can you confirm whether this is a platform-side issue or something we should address in our client config? We have traffic pinned to crest5b:latest with default batching.

Thanks — this is impacting a production cohort, happy to jump on a call.

Sam
Customer Ops | BrightLayer
sam.torres@brightlayer.app

[attachment: crest5b-sample-logs-20261214.tar.gz]

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@brightlayer.app>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 08:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Crest5b production timeouts (us-west) — urgent

Sam — thanks for the quick heads-up and for the logs. We've opened internal incident INC-20261214-002 and kicked off a triage with serving and runtime teams. Immediate ask: can you confirm the percent of total traffic in the affected cluster coming from BL (rough estimate is fine), and whether you saw any recent model pin/rollout changes?

Short-term actions we're applying now:
- Temporarily increase autoscaler target for the us-west crest5b pool (should reduce queueing).
- Enable an emergency fallback route to crest5b-fallback (smaller variant) for requests that exceed 800ms backend latency.
- Our engineers will review the logs you sent and follow up within the hour with a mitigation status update.

I will keep you posted in this thread; if you prefer a call, I can loop in Ben and Karthik.

—Evelyn

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Torres <sam.torres@brightlayer.app>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Crest5b production timeouts (us-west) — triage notes

Evelyn / team — quick triage notes from runtime:
- Observed elevated tail-latency and 5xx spike starting 07:48 PST; correlated with a high churn of prefix KV cache entries across a subset of T4/P4d hosts in us-west-2.
- Preliminary root cause hypothesis: a recently-deployed KV cache eviction heuristic (rolled 2026-12-13 22:30 UTC) was too aggressive for the request mixing pattern BrightLayer sends, causing increased cold-starts of KV pages and more synchronous CPU work per request.

Mitigation applied at 08:50 PST:
- Reverted the eviction heuristic to the previous policy for the us-west crest5b pool.
- Bumped pool capacity by 20% and adjusted batching to a slightly smaller max-batch to reduce tail latency.
- Stepped up circuit-breaker thresholds and enabled the crest5b-fallback route (as Evelyn noted).

Impact so far: 5xx rate down from ~12% to ~1.3% in the last 10 minutes; median latency improved and tail latencies trending toward normal. We'll continue monitoring for 2 hours and produce an incident timeline and a suggested follow-on fix (likely a tuned eviction policy and a model-variant routing rule).

Attaching a short mitigation runbook we used.

Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. SRE, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
[attachment: mitigation-runbook.pdf]

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@brightlayer.app>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Crest5b: recovery update and next steps

Hi Sam / Priya —

Update: our mitigations (revert eviction heuristic, capacity bump, fallback routing) appear to have stabilized traffic in us-west. We observed the 5xx rate fall to ~1% and tail latencies return to baseline within ~30 minutes of the revert. We're keeping the fallback route active for an additional 6 hours as a precaution.

Planned follow-ups:
1) Postmortem / RCA: we'll share a full timeline and the root cause analysis by EOD tomorrow (2026-12-15). It will include the exact code change that triggered the eviction regression, a proposed fix, and a rollout plan with canary gating.
2) Configuration suggestion: for BrightLayer's workload we recommend pinning crest5b to a conservatively-tuned cache policy or enabling a short grace TTL on KV pages; we can help preconfigure this on your account to avoid regression sensitivity.
3) Credit & SLA: because this impacted production traffic, I'll work with our billing team to evaluate a one-off service credit and temporary SLA flexibility for the window 07:48–09:10 PST.

I've attached the incident-timeline.csv we generated (trimmed) and the mitigation runbook excerpt. If you want an ad-hoc call for deeper technical walk-through, Ben and Karthik are available today.

Thanks for the quick reports and for the log bundle — that sped up triage. We'll follow up with the formal postmortem tomorrow.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
[attachments: mitigation-runbook.pdf, incident-timeline.csv]

From: Priya Shah <pshah@brightlayer.app>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Crest5b: recovery update and next steps

Thanks Evelyn and Ben — we see requests succeeding again and the error rate is back to baseline. Appreciate the quick rollback and the temporary fallback; that prevented larger customer impact.

We would like the postmortem to include: a short timeline we can share internally, the specific rollback/patch we'll need to apply on our side (if any), and whether there are recommended alert threshold changes we should adopt. We'll review your suggested cache policy and follow up with a config request.

—Priya
Head of Platform | BrightLayer
